profile.purpose: Test and recommend high-powered outdoor wok burners for restaurant-style stir-frying at home, and explain why burner design matters more than BTU rating.
profile.thesis: For wok cooking, a burner's design and flame placement matter more than its total BTU output. A concentrated central burner with a heat guard, built-in pilot and wok-side gas valve outperforms more powerful wide-ring burners.
key_takeaways: Outdoor burners help with restaurant-style stir-fries by frying instead of steaming food and by producing wok hei, though good Chinese food can be cooked on a home burner.
Five models were tested, including a water-boiling test in the wok.
A 200,000 BTU wide-ring brewing burner took about a minute to heat the water, while the 160,000 BTU Powerflamer took about 45 seconds because its centralized burner wastes less heat out the sides.
Only about 4% of the big burner's energy reaches the wok, against roughly 9–10% for the Powerflamer.
Wide-ring burners heat the whole wok evenly, which gives less control and pushes flame out toward the cook's hands.
The top pick is the Powerflamer 160EI from Outdoorstirfry.com (about $180 plus shipping). It has a heat guard, a built-in pilot and a gas valve at the wok.
The budget pick is the Eastman Outdoors Portable Kahuna (about $130). It produces 65,000 BTU with concentrated flames and is portable with telescoping legs, but it sits a bit low.
65,000 BTU is plenty unless you cook for more than about six to eight people.

outline.title: Why use an outdoor burner
outline.summary: Explains why Chinese restaurants use very powerful burners: frying rather than steaming, and creating wok hei. Notes that home burners can still make good Chinese food.

outline.title: Testing different burner types
outline.summary: Compares wide-ring and centralized burners using a water-boiling test, energy-efficiency figures and infrared observations. Covers the heat-control and hand-burning problems with the Gas One brewing burner.

outline.title: Top recommendation
outline.summary: Presents the Powerflamer 160EI as the top pick. Covers its heat guard, built-in pilot, wok-side gas valve, rust warning and price.

outline.title: Budget portable option
outline.summary: Recommends the cheaper Eastman Outdoors Portable Kahuna. Covers its concentrated 65,000 BTU flame, build, portability, and its low height with ways to mount it higher.

outline.title: Final conclusions
outline.summary: Recaps the two picks and mentions the infrared and cooking footage included in the video.
